claim: Neural and genetic methods consume most computation
originalWording: Neural and genetic methods consume most computation

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Neural networks and genetic algorithms account for more than half of computing work across the intended general computing population.
strict.rationale: Important neural successes by 2019 did not establish majority use across all computation. AI compute has become a major workload, but a global majority depends on the population and unit of work. The directional expansion is substantial; the literal aggregate threshold is not established.

broader.criterion: Massively parallel neural computation becomes the dominant workload driving frontier and hyperscale computing capacity.
broader.rationale: Deep learning was already central to AI research by 2019, but neural workloads only became the dominant driver of frontier supercomputing and hyperscale datacenter buildouts during the 2020s generative-AI wave. Under a charitable frontier-compute scope, this arrived late rather than by 2019.
